translationRepairs: Mao had ridden that horse for years and knew the other man was mistaken; without a word he gave up the animal, hitched his cart himself, and called over his shoulder that if the horse was not truly the man's, he should return it to him at the Chancellor's compound."

Mao had ridden that horse for years and knew the other man was mistaken; without a word he gave up the animal, hitched his cart himself, and called over his shoulder that if the horse was not truly the man's, he should return it to him at the Chancellor's compound.
The idiomatic sentence already reports 顧曰 indirectly, so the terminal closing quotation mark is a stray punctuation error with no matching open quote.
Your chief has always been friendly with that clerk; seasonal gifts between them are simply courtesy."
The pavilion chief has long been a good official; giving him seasonal gifts is proper courtesy."

亭長素善吏 means the pavilion chief has long been a good official; the before text wrongly invents friendliness with another clerk, and the after restores that sense while keeping seasonal gifts (歲時遺之) as proper courtesy.
A pavilion chief borrowed someone's ox and refused to return it; the ox's owner sued Gong.
A pavilion chief borrowed someone's ox and refused to return it; the ox's owner appealed to Gong.
訟於恭 places the complaint before Gong as magistrate; the before text wrongly makes Gong the defendant, while appealed to Gong matches the Chinese and the following summons of the pavilion chief.
The classic states: "The queen issues commands to the four quarters."
The classic states: "The sovereign issues commands to the four quarters."
In the Changes line 後以施令誥四方, 後 is the sovereign/ruler; the next unit glosses it as 君, so queen is a false reading and sovereign is accurate.
As Confucius said: "The Yin revised Xia ritual and the Zhou revised Yin—each tweak can be traced."
Hence it is said: "The Yin inherited Xia ritual and the Zhou inherited Yin ritual—each adjustment can be traced."
The Chinese only has 故曰 and 殷因於夏禮…; naming Confucius invents an attribution, and inherited/adjustment correctly renders 因 and 損益.
The following year Emperor He died; Wei supervised work on Empress Dowager Dou's Shun tomb.
The following year Emperor He died; Wei supervised construction of the Shun Mausoleum.
典作順陵 names only supervision of the Shun Mausoleum; Empress Dowager Dou is invented English and is rightly removed.
He often quoted Confucius: "Lead only with punishments and people stay out of trouble but feel no shame."
He often took as principle: "Lead only with punishments and people stay out of trouble but feel no shame."
常以為 presents the saying as Liu Kuan's principle; the Chinese does not name Confucius, so quoted Confucius invents a speaker and took as principle restores the source wording.
The emperor asked whether the Grand Commandant was drunk."
The emperor asked whether the Grand Commandant was drunk.
The idiomatic line paraphrases 帝問 without opening quotes, so the final closing quotation mark is stray punctuation.

The maid panicked; Liu's expression never changed as he asked softly whether she had burned her hand.
The idiomatic line already turns 羹爛汝手？ into indirect speech, so the terminal closing quotation mark is a stray mark with no matching opener.
